subject: FORGE FINALE 47 -- sample counts complete, payoff half honestly at 24/118
body:
FORGE FINALE session 47 -- every rate report now says how many trades it came from. 34 of 119 this morning, 118 of 118 now.

Two of the last fifteen turned out not to be win rates at all. One printed "calibWR" from a field that is declared once, read once, and assigned nowhere in sixty-three thousand lines -- it has always printed zero, sitting in a line about a threshold change, with nothing to tell a reader it wasn't measured. The other printed "WR 62%" when the number was actually "62% of the way from the floor win rate to the target" -- a normalised alignment score wearing a win-rate label. Both fixed; the dead field left declared with a note so the finding stays visible.

But I am NOT marking the criterion done, and the reason is worth telling you. It asks for two things: the sample count AND the realised payoff. I was one step from calling it met when I checked the payoff half -- and found the check for it was a regex that reported 119 of 119 passing. It could not fail: a bare "R" matches almost anywhere, and "profit" matches any comment. Rewritten to require a payoff figure actually formatted into the line, the honest answer is 24 of 118, not 118.

So: count half complete and verified, payoff half at 24 of 118. Retrofitting the rest is not a repeat of today's work -- many of those lines have no realised payoff in scope at all, and inventing one would be exactly the failure this criterion exists to prevent. Next session triages which is which.

Still 30/45. Two sessions now without a criterion gained, so the next one has to land one or the campaign's own stall rule stops it to reassess. Build SLS(179), 0 errors 0 warnings, byte-identical across all three locations, terminal never running.
